head: b7ee4555810dcb82b4a0714200c599ab076daac8
summary: Maintainers can authorize agent merges without required checks through a head-specific confirmation while retaining other gates. Maintenance is bounded; real-use impact and complete instruction-growth measurements remain unknown.
reasons: The change directly addresses #551: maintainers can authorize an agent to merge a verified Ask-mode PR when neither GitHub nor the trusted seam requires checks.
The confirmation excuses only an empty check set for the submitted head. Other readiness gates remain, and the result records the confirmed head.
Maintenance stays bounded: one flag, a head comparison, result evidence, an initialization warning, and focused tests. No dependency or configuration setting is added.

The added instruction explains a non-obvious authorization decision that Ruby cannot establish. SKILL.md loads the complete workflow on every delivery task, so the approximately 30 added words impose a recurring cost.

The required instruction-growth report is absent; the packet supplies only an approximate workflow delta. Complete rendered word and byte costs remain unverified, but the inspected addition does not demonstrate material instruction growth or duplication.

Three review rounds fixed one risk; two CodeRabbit findings were also reported fixed. The three remaining findings are described only as nits, so their substance cannot be independently assessed. Real-use benefit and incident frequency remain unknown.
alternative: Keep the bounded confirmation path. Requiring maintainers to click GitHub merge would preserve the reported friction; adding required checks changes repository policy rather than repairing Ask-mode delivery.
next_action: Attach the existing instruction-growth output and the three documented nit dispositions to complete the review evidence.
